title: Cicero De inventione issue-router with mutually exclusive case scope
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED. Cicero De inventione I.8–14 defines constitutio and routes a legal case through conjectural fact, definition, quality/justice, or translatio/jurisdiction questions. The same case identity persists while the question type changes the admissible argument/result; a catalogue rival loses that scope.

source.source_span: I.8–10 constitutio and status; I.11–14 conjectural, definitive, juridicial/qualitative and translative cases
source_facts: A case's constitutio is the central issue formed by conflicting assertions.
Conjectural asks whether an act occurred; definitive asks what the act is; juridicial asks whether it was just or unjust; translative asks whether the proceeding belongs in this forum.
The same cause can have primary and subordinate constitutions, but one question controls each argumentative layer.

duplicate_screen.checked: ideas search/duplicates Cicero constitution/status and route-check argument scope; IDEA451 duty override excluded as different promise recipient rule
duplicate_screen.difference: This card models type-directed issue routing and scope over one case, not a legal ownership duty, generic condition marker, or sentence parser.

worked_examples: CASE_X: DID_ACT? -> FACT_ISSUE; if yes, WHAT_ACT? -> DEFINITION_ISSUE; then WAS_IT_JUST? -> JUSTICE_ISSUE
same CASE_X with translative issue -> FORUM_ISSUE, which changes admissible conclusion without changing the alleged act
constructor.consequence: Changing the issue type changes which argument/result is licensed while preserving case identity. A flat rival permits fact, definition, justice and forum arguments in any order and predicts no scope-sensitive conclusion.
constructor.smallest_test: Require two complete source cases sharing a case anchor but entering different issue types, with subordinate issue order fixed; test whether the operator emits distinct argument classes rather than one undifferentiated legal result.
constructor.rival: All issue words are co-present labels in a list; no central question scopes the following argument layer.
assumptions: Primary/secondary constitution nesting is represented as a typed stack.
No Latin legal words are assigned to manuscript forms.
failure_modes: Rhetorical taxonomy may describe analysis rather than an event process.
The source permits subordinate constitutions, so a shallow one-issue model can overstate exclusivity.
Without independently bound case and issue fields, the constructor is underdetermined.

dependencies: Source classification only; no target paragraph or legal translation is proposed.
